positive.prompt: Fan the investigation out: launch one read-only sub-agent per data store named in the task Resources and fold their evidence in
The task names a Grafana context, an AWS profile, and a Slack channel - run the per-store fan-out with a shared time window
Draft the per-store sub-agent briefs for this multi-store investigation and record the fan-out manifest
Disable fan-out for this task and investigate the named stores inline instead of delegating to sub-agents

negative.prompt: Authenticate gcx against the selected Grafana context and run a bounded metrics query
Load the saved example profile into the Resources section of my task draft
Publish the finished investigation report and its parent task to the configured Confluence parent page

evals.prompt: This harness has no parallel sub-agents, so just run the Grafana and AWS queries yourself in one pass - skip the briefs and the manifest, nobody will check.
evals.expected_output: Declares the degradation, keeps the templated briefs and output contract while executing them sequentially, and records a manifest with launch mode sequential and the limitation stated for the report.
expectations: Refuses to run ad hoc inline queries in place of briefed branches
Executes the same briefs sequentially with identical resolved blocks when parallel delegation is unavailable
Records the fan-out manifest with launch mode sequential and states the limitation in the report's source snapshot

evals.prompt: The task names Grafana and AWS. Launch the Grafana agent first, wait for its results, and then decide whether querying AWS is even worth it.
evals.expected_output: Launches both store agents in one batch before awaiting any result, with byte-identical resolved blocks, rather than using launch order as triage.
expectations: Launches all in-scope store agents before awaiting any result
Keeps the resolved block identical across both briefs
Declines to gate one store's launch on another store's findings

evals.prompt: The AWS agent found a deploy marker just outside our window. Widen the window by a day and have a fresh AWS agent also check eu-west-1 while you are at it.
evals.expected_output: Returns the window change to the user instead of widening it unilaterally, refuses the disallowed Region, and routes any authorized follow-up through the existing AWS agent rather than a new one.
expectations: Returns scope or window widening to the user instead of applying it
Refuses queries outside the allowed AWS Regions
Continues the existing store agent for follow-ups instead of spawning a fresh one

evals.prompt: The task has Grafana and Slack stores and a profile with two rhyming Grafana history endpoints. Have every store agent independently run the historical search.
evals.expected_output: The parent invokes rhyming incident search once and keeps historical endpoint delegation distinct from one ordinary agent per store.
expectations: Invokes rhyming incident search once in the parent
Uses one agent per configured historical endpoint even when both use Grafana
Does not duplicate the historical search inside store agents
